title: BaseSubgraph exposes four throwing assertCan* helpers plus a non-throwing canReadDocument for list filtering
content:
## The enforcement surface

All of these are public methods on `BaseSubgraph`. The `ph generate subgraph` scaffold hands you the instance as the `subgraph` parameter of `getResolvers`, so you call them as `subgraph.assertCanRead(...)`. Class-field resolvers call them on `this` instead — that is the style the built-in subgraphs use, and both forms reach the same public methods.

| Helper | Use when | On failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assertCanRead(identifier, ctx)` | Reading one document the caller named (id or slug) | throws `Forbidden` |
| `assertCanWrite(identifier, ctx)` | Mutating one document the caller named | throws `Forbidden` |
| `assertCanExecuteOperation(identifier, type, ctx)` | Executing a specific operation type on a document | throws `Forbidden` |
| `assertCanCreate(ctx)` | Creating a genuinely top-level document with no parent | throws `Forbidden` |
| `canReadDocument(canonicalId, ctx)` | Filtering a list — non-throwing read check on an id from the data layer | returns `boolean` |
| `authorizationService.isSupremeAdmin(address)` | Short-circuiting per-item filtering for policy-wide callers | returns `boolean` |

Note the sixth row: `isSupremeAdmin` is reached through `subgraph.authorizationService`, not directly on the subgraph.

## Details worth knowing

Every `assertCan*` that takes an `identifier` returns an `AuthorizedDocumentHandle`; use its `fetchIdentifier` for the subsequent fetch. There are also lower-level `*Canonical` variants (`assertCanReadCanonical` and friends) used by the built-in subgraphs when the data layer has already resolved an id — prefer the identifier-accepting variants in your own code.

`assertCanCreate` is narrower than it looks. When creating a document **under a parent**, the meaningful check is write access on that parent, so `assertCanWrite(parentIdentifier, ctx)` is the right call; reserve `assertCanCreate` for top-level documents.

Supporting types exported from `@powerhousedao/reactor-api`: `Context`, `CanonicalDocumentId`, `AuthorizationPolicy`, `AuthorizedDocumentHandle`, `IAuthorizationService`.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/03-Build/03-BuildingUserExperiences/07-Authorization/05-EnforcingAuthorizationInSubgraphs.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: assertCanRead/Write/ExecuteOperation/Create throw Forbidden; canReadDocument returns a boolean. isSupremeAdmin lives on subgraph.authorizationService, not on the subgraph itself.
